Rack Inventory
rack-vlm-lab

Rack inventory, read from photographs

A detector finds each device in a rack photo and measures it. A vision-language model reads what is printed on its face. This is what the two together produced — and how far it can be trusted.

1  The racks 2  Every device 3  How reliable is this

1  The racks

What is installed, in mounting order. The photo beside each rack shows where every device was found. Port counts marked model number were taken from the part number rather than the detector, because a number printed on the metal beats one inferred from a hundred-pixel strip.

2  Every device

Pick any device for the full entry: what it is, how it is cabled, what it does, and what a technician should still check on site.

3  How reliable is this

The same crops were read by several models and prompts. Where they all agree, the answer is solid. Where they split, it is not — and those crops are listed first.

Port counts and positions come from the detector unless marked otherwise; makes and models come from the reader. What a cable connects to is not shown, because the far end is outside the photograph.
